 ‘I just wanted to kill Colin Kaepernick’: Vernon Davis blames Kaepernick, not Kam Chancellor, for his 2012 concussion hit 
 Vernon Davis knows who to blame. 
 Sayed 
 | 
 Published: Nov 1, 2026 02:45 pm 
 Former 49ers tight end Vernon Davis recently discussed a well-known 2012 hit on the Uninterrupted Weekly  podcast. According to Essentially Sports , he said his immediate reaction after the play was directed at the quarterback who threw the ball rather than the defender who delivered the contact. “When I got up, I just wanted to kill Colin Kaepernick. That’s what I wanted to do. I wasn’t worried about Kam Chancellor; I wanted to go after Colin Kaepernick,” Davis said.
 He confirmed that he viewed the throw from Kaepernick as a hospital ball, a term used for a pass that leaves the receiver exposed to a hard hit. The play took place during the 49ers’ visit to Seattle on December 23 in Week 16 of the 2012 season. San Francisco lost that game 42-13.
 Late in the first quarter, Kaepernick threw toward Davis, who was open along the right sideline. Seattle safety Kam Chancellor closed quickly and made contact just after the catch, forcing the ball loose. Davis suffered a concussion and did not return.

 Officials called unnecessary roughness on Chancellor and assessed a 10-yard penalty. Seattle later blocked a 49ers field goal attempt at the end of the drive and returned it for a touchdown. Davis said the physical contact itself was not what troubled him most. “It wasn’t even the hit that bothered me; it was more of the whiplash. The hit, it didn’t hurt,” he explained. He described going straight to the locker room instead of the sideline.
 In a 2017 appearance for the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Washington, Davis talked about the effects. He said he “lost [his] memory a little bit.” He recounted not knowing what had happened right away. “I just didn’t know what happened. I was like, ‘Wow I just got hit by a very big man.’ He hit me hard. You know what somebody told me? He said, ‘Shake it off. It’s all right. Shake it off.’ I’m like, ‘I can’t remember anything. You tell me to shake it off? Why don’t you go shake it off, buddy?’ That was quite a hit,” Davis said.
 Chancellor spoke after the game about the defense’s approach. “As defensive backs, we said it’s going to start with us in the back, coming out there being physical and just setting the tone,” he said. “I think we set the tone today.” Seahawks coach Pete Carroll addressed the flag. “That hit on the sidelines was so vicious that they just had to throw the flag; something must be wrong; you can’t hit somebody that hard. But as it turned out, you look at it and you go, ‘What’s the problem?’ So we’ll find out from the league what they think,” Carroll said. He indicated he hoped the play would be viewed as an example of a legal hit.
 Chancellor said officials told him he had lunged illegally, though available video appeared to show shoulder-to-chest contact. The NFL did not issue a fine for the play. Chancellor later helped Seattle win Super Bowl XLVIII by a score of 43-8 over the Denver Broncos and earned four Pro Bowl selections. His career ended after a neck injury in 2017, and the Seahawks terminated his contract in 2019 after he failed a physical.
 Davis was already an established player when the 49ers drafted Kaepernick. The two continued to work together on the field. In 2012, Kaepernick’s first season as the full-time starter, Davis finished second among the team’s pass-catchers with 548 receiving yards. Kaepernick’s time in the league later ended in controversy, and he has since shared his side of his NFL exit . The 49ers traded Davis to the Denver Broncos midway through the 2015 season, and he played for Washington the following year.
 Davis returned the next week against the Arizona Cardinals and caught for five yards. By the postseason he was healthy again and recorded 254 receiving yards along with one touchdown. Kaepernick, meanwhile, believes he could outplay current QBs  even though he hasn’t been watching NFL games.
